correctness.rationale: For each dimension \(d\ge2\) and positive prices and budget \(P,Q,B>0\), the strict trace-inverse Hessian on connected hypercube Laplacians and injective edge representation give the unique unrestricted global optimum. Price-preserving automorphisms force two positive conductance classes. The weighted Walsh spectrum has eigenvalues \(2(ky+\epsilon x)\) with binomial multiplicities. The exact scalar objective \(F_N\) and its derivative are derived. Binomial concentration gives \(A_N=2^N(2/N+O(N^{-2}))\) and the second reciprocal sum \(2^N(4/N^2+O(N^{-3}))\), with third-moment control. In the premium case \(P>Q\), the derivative root satisfies \(r^2\sim N^2Q/[4(P-Q)2^N]\); for a discounted direction \(P<Q\), the normalized derivative has the unique positive root \((\sqrt{2Q/P-1}-1)/2\); equal prices force \(r=1\). The standalone verify.py passed 13 exact symbolic identities and 556 numerical checks. Limits, boundary cases and normalization were cross-checked in the self-review; no independent audit has occurred.

value.rationale: Single-coordinate differential pricing is a natural minimal heterogeneity of hypercube interconnection design, under a standard all-pairs resistance objective. An expensive direction remains necessary for graph connectivity but receives exponentially vanishing relative conductance; a cheap direction instead becomes linearly more heavily weighted. The opposite rates and constants are usable in dimension-dependent budget planning and numerical optimization benchmarks, and are not a relabeling of the equal-price hypercube trace or routine fixed-weight graph-index computation.
